articles.title: SEC fines Kentucky $500,000 for field storming after win over LSU
articles.summary: The Wildcats moved to 5-1 with the 35-34 overtime win.
articles.body:
Kentucky is the first school to get a fine from the SEC for field storming in 2026.

The conference announced its obligatory $500,000 fine of the Wildcats on Sunday afternoon after fans entered the field after UK's 35-34 overtime win over LSU .

The SEC announced in the spring of 2025 that fines had been upped from $250,000 to $500,000 for a school's first field storm of the season. The fines are designed to keep fans from entering the playing field — or court — after a win when the opposing team and officials are still present. Fans are allowed to go onto the playing surface after those people have left for the locker rooms.

The win was Kentucky's second consecutive 35-34 overtime win. In Week 5, the Wildcats beat South Carolina by the same score on a 2-point conversion. Saturday night, quarterback Kenny Minchey ran it in for the game-winning conversion.

After the game, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin said he expected Kentucky to go for the win.

Kentucky moved to 5-1 with the victory and is now No. 15 in the AP Top 25. LSU (4-2) fell from No. 12 to No. 22.

While LSU has won more than two-thirds of its games against the Wildcats dating back to 1949, it hasn't won in Lexington since a 33-30 win in 2002. LSU also hasn't won an SEC game on the road since beating Arkansas in October 2024. Since then, the Tigers are on an eight-game losing streak.

articles.title: Ramis: "Entiendo que en el campo tengas la duda, pero el VAR ha visto la imagen y es clarísima, es roja"
articles.standfirst: El técnico rojillo reclama una posible expulsión de Natan justo antes del 4-2 de Isco
articles.summary: El técnico rojillo reclama una posible expulsión de Natan justo antes del 4-2 de Isco
articles.body: Luis Miguel Ramis, técnico de Osasuna, se mostró decepcionado por la derrota de su equipo en La Cartuja frente al Betis pero, sobre todo, lamentó lo que a su juicio fueron dos graves errores arbitrales: en el penalti con el que Isco abrió el marcador y en una jugada en la segunda parte en la que los rojillos pidieron roja directa para Natan y en cuya continuación el capitán verdiblanco hizo el 4-2 que terminó de frustrar el intento de reacción navarra. Logró meterse en el partido tras el 3-0: "El partido había que defenderlo sin balón, obviamente porque el rival te exige mucho, y también con balón. En la primera parte lo hemos intentado; ese bloque bajo no nos estaba generando muchos problemas. Para mí el penalti es muy riguroso porque es una acción en la que se gira un jugador, propio de la acción de la cobertura, y nada más rozarle pues el otro jugador se va al suelo y lo pita. No estábamos haciendo las cosas tan mal como para ir perdiendo. Luego el 2-0 viene de un error que tenemos que solucionar porque nos está poniendo muy cuesta arriba los partidos. En la segunda parte hemos entrado bien, ahí hemos tenido la mala suerte del tercer gol en ese doble rechace y la acción que podía haber cambiado el signo del partido claramente". La polémica con Natan: "Yo lo acabo de ver ahora mismo y me imagino que en el VAR la habrán visto. Obviamente Natan no quiere interrumpir la carrera de Rubén, pero Rubén lo hace muy bien y se cruza. Cuando un jugador se cruza no hay situaciones involuntarias, no hay penaltis involuntarios; nadie quiere hacer penalti, pero si te cruzas y lo tocas, el jugador va al suelo. Lo he visto ahora mismo: es verdad que se cruzan en la trayectoria, pero ahí no tienes que valorar la inercia de la carrera, simplemente que hay un jugador delante tuyo, se te cruza muy bien y va al suelo porque hay un contacto. Es clarísima, es roja, que con ese 3-2 podía haber cambiado el signo del partido, y sigo sin entender ese tipo de decisiones". Posible segunda jugada: "Una segunda jugada, ninguna. El balón va a la espalda, Rubén está por delante, le gana y al cruzarse se produce el contacto, ya está. Ahí no hay voluntariedad por parte de Natan porque no quiere interrumpirle la carrera, pero al cruzarse chocan, se rozan y va al suelo. Y yo lo acabo de ver ahora, no admite interpretación. Si se ve en el VAR... puede ser que en el campo tengas la duda de si en ese cruce ha habido contacto, esto lo entiendo por parte del colegiado, pero en el VAR he visto la imagen y es muy claro que hay contacto. Por lo tanto, aun sin querer, la situación es muy clara de roja y expulsión". Decisiones que les están perjudicando: "Ya me gustaría decir lo contrario, pero sí. Tenemos que mirarnos a nosotros también porque nos están haciendo muchos goles y muchos por errores que son solventables, pero es verdad que no estamos teniendo fortuna en ese tipo de decisiones. Ya van en ocho jornadas, tres de ellas muy importantes en las que ya no es favorecernos, es que nos den lo que ha pasado en el partido, nada más". Cómo levantar la moral de su equipo: "Con tranquilidad, descansando. La segunda parte ha sido buena, hemos dominado y hemos tenido al rival con muchas dudas. Lástima no haber mantenido un poquito más ese 3-2 que ha venido producto de la acción polémica de la roja, y en la siguiente acción ha venido el gol. Haciéndoles ver que hacen muchas cosas bien, pese al resultado que muchas veces es a lo primero a lo que te vas. Nuestra obligación como técnicos es hacer un análisis de las cosas que hacemos bien, que son muchas, y estoy seguro de que cuando haces eso, persistes, insistes y los jugadores creen como así es, se sale adelante y tendremos premio pronto".

articles.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin Reveals What Official Told Him About Not Blowing Whistle on Kentucky Tush-Push TD
articles.summary: Kentucky scored on a controversial Tush Push touchdown at the end of the first half during Saturday's 35-34 overtime win over LSU, when quarterback Kenny Minchey appeared to have his momentum halted but officials swallowed their whistles, allowing him to score on a second surge over the goal line.
articles.body:
Kentucky scored on a controversial Tush Push touchdown at the end of the first half during Saturday's 35-34 overtime win over LSU, when quarterback Kenny Minchey appeared to have his momentum halted but officials swallowed their whistles, allowing him to score on a second surge over the goal line.

LSU head coach Lane Kiffin told reporters on Sunday that an official said there was "just too much at stake" to blow the play dead right away.

"(The line judge) said he'd be killed if he would have blown the whistle for the play being stopped, even though it appeared to be stopped," he added.

Kiffin said the context of the moment shouldn't have influenced the call.

"Don't not blow [the whistle] because it was such a big play," he told reporters.

"The rules are the rules, so if you see it that way, then see it that way," he continued. "That's my complaint with it. It all comes down to just blowing the whistle, so it is what it is."

The loss dropped LSU to 4-2 on the season and put their College Football Playoff hopes on life control, with tough matchups against Mississippi State, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee still to come.

articles.body: KOLKATA: India head coach Crispin Chettri was seen making a solemn gesture of disappointment on the touchline when Darina Ishmukhametova gave Russia the breakthrough in the 22nd minute at Kishore Bharati Krirangan here on Sunday.Despite Russia head coach Yuri Krasnozhan retaining only two players from the starting line-up that secured a 4-0 win in the first friendly on Thursday, the visitors once again showcased their class and quality, beating hosts India 8-0 in the second ‘unofficial’ international match.For the opening 21 minutes, the Indians virtually parked the bus in their own half and managed to keep the relentless Russian attacks at bay, thanks largely to some determined defending, especially from Ranjana Chanu. articles.title: Swansea City's humble approach under Matos paying off - Ben Cabango
articles.summary: Ben Cabango believes the Championship leaders' ethos is paying dividends as they go into games against Millwall and West Ham United.
articles.body:
Ben Cabango believes Swansea City's "humble" approach is paying dividends as they look forward to games against Millwall and West Ham United sitting top of the Championship.

The Wales defender helped his side once again hit back from 1-0 down, this time to beat Norwich , as the league campaign resumed following a four-game international break.

Cabango says boss Vitor Matos' ethos is paying off and building confidence at the Swansea.com Stadium.

"The main thing is we can feel real togetherness and the character," said the club's 26-year-old skipper.

"I feel like that's the third time I think we've come back from 1-0 nil down this season. I don't think there's ever any panic when we do go one-nil down."

Swansea have lost just once this season - away at Southampton - and have three wins and two draws at home.

"There's real belief right now in the squad, and we're playing with that confidence, aggression, like constantly, and that comes from the gaffer," added Cabango.

"Every game, he's always saying 'treat the next game like the cup final' and we don't look too far ahead.

"We're a humble squad and just pushing to get better every day."

Toshack watches on as Matos' Swans eye own history

Haaland 'gave me his shirt... but didn't take mine'

Iconic Swansea manager John Toshack was there to see the comeback against Norwich, with Cabango acknowledging excitement among their fans at leading the promotion race cannot be ignored.

"I can already feel that, to be honest with you. The Swans fans [and] us as a team, we obviously are excited.

"But we've had a real good start. It's given us a great platform to build off, and we've just got to carry on."

Doing so will mean heading to Millwall on Tuesday - before hosting third-placed West Ham on Saturday - under no illusions as to what lies ahead.

"We know what to expect going to Millwall away," said Cabango.

"It's always going to be a physical, demanding game and the set pieces, the long balls. It's going to be a tough test and a different one to today [against Norwich].

"But we're going to obviously recover, prepare for it, and go in with that confidence and belief, like we do."

Cabango confident after intense Wales duty

On a personal level, it also means no let-up for Cabango after returning from top-tier Nations League duty that saw Wales lose to Portugal then Denmark twice, while also claiming Norway's scalp.

Cabango returned to club action feeling "confident" having earned wide praise for the way he marshalled Erling Haaland during Wales' win against Norway.

"Four games in two weeks is always going to be hard, and playing against the opposition you do, it's really intense," said Cabango.

He believes Swansea shook off their international-break "rustiness" against Norwich after an extended period away from domestic football.

"We came looking a new team really, and it was real positive to come from a goal behind and get the three points," he added.

articles.title: 20 goals in three matches! India U17 women make history, become first-ever Indian side to qualify for back-to-back Asian Cups
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s U17 women’s side scripted history on Sunday, becoming the first-ever Indian side to qualify for back-to-back Women’s Asian Cups in any
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s U17 women’s side scripted history on Sunday, becoming the first-ever Indian side to qualify for back-to-back Women’s Asian Cups in any age category, including the senior level, after a commanding 4-0 victory over Malaysia in their final Group E match of the AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup qualifiers in Selayang, Malaysia.The Young Tigresses, coached by Joakim Alexandersson, delivered another impressive performance at the MP Selayang Stadium to seal their place in the AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup China 2027. Redima Devi Chingkhamayum opened the scoring in the first half before Pritika Barman, Anushka Kumari and substitute Nidhi struck after the break to complete a dominant win.India finished their qualifying campaign with a perfect record of nine points from three matches, scoring 20 goals without conceding once. They had opened their campaign with a staggering 14-0 demolition of Iraq before registering a 2-0 victory over Syria.Malaysia finished second in Group E with six points, while Syria and Iraq followed behind.Redima breaks the deadlock after India's sustained pressureHeavy rain had left the pitch slushy, with puddles across the playing surface making it difficult for both sides to maintain the flow of their passing moves. However, the conditions did little to disrupt India’s attacking intent as the Young Tigresses dominated possession and repeatedly threatened the Malaysian goal.The Indian midfield kept the pressure on through a steady supply of through balls, while the wide players stretched the opposition defence with dangerous crosses. Silky Devi Sorokhaibam operated effectively down the right, with Alva providing width from the left. Nira Chanu Longjam came close to opening the scoring, only to see her header strike the crossbar.India won nine corners in the first half as Malaysia’s defence struggled to contain the relentless pressure. The hosts were kept in the contest by goalkeeper Putri Aina Husna Binto Mohd Subri, who produced several important saves.The breakthrough finally arrived in the 29th minute. Redima collected a pass from Silky and unleashed a powerful right-footed strike that flew into the middle of the net, giving India a deserved lead.The Young Tigresses continued to push for a second goal before the interval. Anushka beat the advancing goalkeeper, but her effort was cleared off the line by Nina Binti Hasmaji.Three second-half goals seal historic qualificationIndia maintained their attacking momentum after the restart, with Subri again denying substitute Pritika and Anushka with timely interventions.The resistance was eventually broken when Alva found Anushka in space. The forward unselfishly rolled the ball across to Pritika on the right, and the substitute drove a low right-footed shot into the net to double India’s advantage.Anushka then added a third with her eighth goal of the qualifying campaign. Following another Indian corner, she picked up a clearance and unleashed a long-range effort from the right that dipped into the near post, leaving the goalkeeper with little chance.Malaysia managed a few forward moves late in the match, but goalkeeper Munni and centre-backs Julan Nongmaithem and Abhista Basnett ensured India’s clean sheet remained intact.The final goal belonged to Nidhi, who scored her first-ever international goal in memorable fashion. The substitute embarked on a solo run from around 25 yards out, weaved past three defenders, rounded the onrushing goalkeeper and finished from close range to complete the 4-0 victory.The final whistle sparked jubilant celebrations among the Indian players and support staff, capping an unbeaten qualifying campaign and a landmark achievement for Indian women’s football. articles.title: Amidst the storm, a Manchester City midfielder stood up and set the tone at Anfield
articles.summary: Manchester City picked up an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield yesterday. Enzo Maresca’s side won their eighth consecutive match in all competitions...
articles.body:
Manchester City picked up an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield yesterday. Enzo Maresca's side won their eighth consecutive match in all competitions and look to have created a siege mentality from this point onwards. However, City didn't have it their own way at Anfield. Ryan Gravenberch picking up a second yellow card in the 62nd minute and was sent off. From that point onwards, City ruthlessly dispatched Andoni Iraola's side. However, to begin the game, City didn't make the strongest of starts. When they were down it was Elliot Anderson who stood up and set the tone for his team.

It was Elliot Anderson who stood up and lifted Manchester City at Anfield yesterday.

Liverpool began yesterday's match well, especially in the opening ten minutes. Andoni Iraola's side did look up for the occasion, while Manchester City took time to find their feet. When City needed someone to begin to make a positive impact in yesterday's match, it was Elliot Anderson who stood up to be counted.

Elliot Anderson led the way as Manchester City gradually grabbed control of possession in midfield in the first half of yesterday's match. He threw himself into challenges and set about destroying Liverpool's early momentum. Anderson was also a key component as Enzo Maresca's side settled into the match. His passing was on point, and in truth, there were shades of Rodri in Anderson's display. It would take until the second half for City to take control of yesterday's match before they ran away with it.

At the heart of it all was Elliot Anderson. He was Manchester City's man-of-the-match yesterday. The statistics below highlight Anderson's influence on yesterday's match. Anderson's tone-setting display is even more remarkable when you consider that he is still finding his feet as a Manchester City player. To thrive in an environment like yesterday's speaks volumes about a players quality. Elliot Anderson is a special player as his performance yesterday illustrated.

Elliot Anderson believes that this City squad is now closer together as yesterday's win illustrated.

Enzo Maresca's side overcame all of the outside noise to pick up a massive 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield yesterday. There was a real sense of togetherness that shone through in Manchester City's performance. Speaking after his man-of-the-match display at Anfield, Elliot Anderson said that the unity of this City squad has never been stronger. In an interview with mancity.com , Anderson said: " We're all so together, more together than ever. And I think we have to be like that. We've got to stick together. And I think it really brings us together I think. It gives you that determination to come out here, everyone is against you, and turn them over, which we did. "

Elliot Anderson lifted his team when they needed it against Liverpool yesterday. It was Anderson who stood up and embodied the togetherness of this Manchester City side that he spoke of. Anderson arrived at City as one of the elite midfielders in the Premier League. Based on his display yesterday, and his early season form, Anderson is well on his way to further enhancing his reputation. Elite players lift their team in a hostile environment. That is exactly what Elliot Anderson did against Liverpool.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Honors Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin With T-Shirt
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers picked up an impressive win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5. The veteran quarterback tossed three touchdowns...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers picked up an impressive win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5. The veteran quarterback tossed three touchdowns in the 34-22 win, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and a touchdown.

The vibes were good in Pittsburgh as the Steelers improved to 3-0 at home on the season. Rodgers even decided to have some fun in his postgame press conference by wearing a special T-shirt.

Rodgers appeared at the podium with a shirt that featured the letters "DGBTTF," prompting questions of what it meant. The quarterback explained it is an homage to Mike Tomlin and his phrase, "Don't get beat to the flat."

The clip was shown to Tomlin on the Sunday Night Football pregame show on NBC.

A quick search of the phrase on X reveals it being said by Tomlin during his tenure with the Steelers. Rodgers did clarify that it was not a warning to the Colts defense, but rather a nice shoutout for his former head coach. Tomlin always had a catchphrase at the ready and it's clear his players took his words to heart.

The Steelers defense did a great job of listening to the phrase by keeping the Colts offense in check, which included holding Jonathan Taylor to 45 rushing yards.

Last Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns was a rough one for the Steelers. Rodgers was seen shouting at head coach Mike McCarthy and national storylines emerged about how that could impact the entire team. The veteran quarterback did throw three touchdowns, but he also had two interceptions in the frustrating loss.

Rodgers ultimately kept a clean sheet against the Colts and allowed Warren, Pat Freiermuth, and Germie Bernard to thrive in the passing game. Freiermuth caught two touchdowns, while Warren had a thrilling 80-yard touchdown reception.

The only weak spot in the passing game was DK Metcalf, who had to deal with Sauce Gardner all game. Yet Rodgers was able to spread the ball around with ease.

That explains Rodgers having some fun with his shirt in the postgame press conference. His great performance brought back a positive atmosphere and makes it clear his bickering with McCarthy is not a lingering issue, at least right now.

The Steelers will head south next week to take on a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that just took down the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels proved he is capable of playing at a high level, and will seek to do so against a tough Steelers defense.

articles.title: ‘Seen enough’: Neville says Carrick must stop persisting with one partnership that simply isn’t working
articles.summary: Gary Neville believes the partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo is simply too unreliable to depend upon long-term.The pair started together for th...
articles.body:
Gary Neville believes the partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo is simply too unreliable to depend upon long-term.

The pair started together for the fifth successive game on Saturday night and struggled when up against a dismal Tottenham Hotspur side.

United drop more points to winless Spurs

To say Spurs went the opening four matches of the season without returning a single goal, they could've led by at least four by the interval at Old Trafford had they been more clinical.

United were being completely torn apart in the middle of the park, allowing the visitors to stroll through and create chance after chance.

Tielemans, in particular, was up against it in the first half, making it no surprise he was the one sacrificed to make way for debutant Carlos Baleba in the 60th minute .

What Neville had to say about Mainoo and Tielemans

While United's display still left much to be desired, Baleba was a bright spark in the closing half an hour, leading Neville to say post-match on Sky Sports: "Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now.

"I'm not calling time on it because that's probably too drastic, but I've seen enough to think that's not a midfield that's dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League."

"I think they are both good players, by the way, individually," he continued . "But sometimes you just have players that don't quite knit together or don't quite suit each other.

"I think when Baleba came on with Mainoo, it looked like there was a lot more energy.

"There's going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip because they are going to a Diego Simeone Atletico Madrid and Elland Road.

"If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out.

"They've got a couple of days to recover, pick themselves up from this, and get going because if they don't get going, it's going to be a worrying few weeks."

articles.title: Kyle Hamilton Injury Update Doesn’t Look Good For Ravens in Return Home vs. Falcons
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons‘ training staff made it to Kyle Hamilton first on Sunday Night Football. The Baltimore Ravens‘ star safety went down after a play, and he...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons' training staff made it to Kyle Hamilton first on Sunday Night Football.

The Baltimore Ravens' star safety went down after a play, and he was closer to Atlanta's sideline, and those trainers sprung into action.

Soon, Hamilton's own trainers were there to see how he was doing, but clearly he was hurt.

It was the last thing Hamilton would've wanted. He's from not far outside Atlanta, and so Sunday Night Football in Week 5 was a bit of a home game for him. He had a lot of supporters in attendance.

They would all be sitting there hoping Hamilton isn't hurt too badly.

Hamilton got himself involved in the tackling situation on a run play for Falcons RB Bijan Robinson .

He ended the play lying face first on the ground.

The trainers attended to him, and they took his helmet away.

The good news is that Hamilton jogged off to the blue medical tent.

If it's a head injury, Hamilton will have to go through concussion protocol and pass it to return to the game.

Hamilton's posture on the field certainly suggested it could've been a head problem, but it also could've been another part of his body that got hurt and caused him to lay prone on the ground for a few moments.

Hamilton is generally viewed as the nickel guy for the Ravens if you talk in traditional defensive terms, but really he's more like a rover. He's allowed to move around the field and make plays wherever he's needed.

By upbringing, Hamilton is more of a safety.

The Ravens have Malaki Starks on the field every play with Hamilton, and they also have the veteran Jaylinn Hawkins who plays a bunch.

The player who might qualify as behind Hamilton on the depth chart is the rookie Chandler Rivers .

Really, though, the Ravens can't do the same things defensively with Hamilton out of the game.

The good news for the Ravens: He came back into the game after just a couple plays missed. He must be just fine.

articles.title: El Rayo, el barrio, Presa
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: “Oscuro e incierto se presentaba el reinado de Witiza”, contaban los manuales escolares de ‘cuando entonces’, como diría Umbral. Así veo ahora el del Rayo Vallecano, propiedad sentimental del Puente de Vallecas, que no es exactamente lo mismo que Vallecas, pero propiedad legal de un señor llamado Raúl Martín Presa, cuyos ingresos vienen en mucha mayor medida (casi un 90%) de la televisión que de la aportación del público en el estadio (10%). Para más complicarlo, la mayoría social del Puente de Vallecas es izquierdista, la facción radical de la hinchada rayista, Los Bukaneros, de extrema izquierda, pero Presa hace alarde de visitantes de Vox en su palco. Y hay un tercer elemento, la Comunidad de Madrid, propietaria del estadio, con la que Martín Presa no ha sabido entenderse. Martín Presa es un hombre extravagante, con una gestión muy sui géneris del club. Sólo le interesa la primera plantilla, y eso lo borda. Nunca antes el Rayo había estado ocho temporadas en Primera, pero el resto es un desastre, desde el abandono de la ciudad deportiva hasta la desatención al correo electrónico. Cometió un error de origen: cuando accedió al Rayo, le dijeron que algunos jugadores habían sido comprados para un partido en el Sánchez-Pizjuán y no tuvo mejor idea que invitar a un grupo de bukaneros para intimidarles. Es notorio que quiere llevarse el club de donde está, hacer un campo mayor en alguna otra zona de Vallecas donde los bukaneros no tendrían tanta presencia ni influencia, pero no encuentra la colaboración de la Comunidad. Martín Presa podría vender el club de forma ventajosa, porque su buena gestión deportiva lo ha valorizado, pero la terquedad es una de sus características más destacadas y entiende que no tiene por qué. Se siente desamparado por la Comunidad y la Policía. Oscuro e incierto se presenta el futuro del Rayo. A ocho meses del Mundial de Brasil, nuestra selección femenina ha aceptado un doble duelo de aúpa ante Estados Unidos en su terreno. El primero se ganó en Washington, 0-2, y fue una pena que quedara ocluido por el del Madrid, a su misma hora, con la conocida peripecia de Vinicius y demás guarnición. Estados Unidos significa muchísimo en el fútbol femenino, fue su gran factor de lanzamiento y ha dominado el escenario hasta ahora. España, campeona mundial vigente, se atreve con todo. ¡Bravo! La retirada de Messi de la selección argentina era un acontecimiento universal que la AFA abarató indecentemente con decisiones frustrantes. Se buscó como rival Benín, selección sin tradición ni presente, en un propósito de abaratar el acontecimiento, dado que Messi ya vendía por sí solo. Y los drones lanzados al cielo plasmaron el anuncio de una empresa de seguros. Un cúmulo de mal gusto para un acontecimiento que hubiera merecido otro envoltorio que ese cochambroso papel de estraza con marca publicitaria.

articles.title: ‘Threw up in my mouth’ – Mike Tomlin explains ‘disgusted’ reaction to Cam Skattebo fumble
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo’s fumble during overtime may have cost the New York Giants the game, but it drew a far more visceral reaction from Mike Tomlin. The Giants ended...
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo's fumble during overtime may have cost the New York Giants the game, but it drew a far more visceral reaction from Mike Tomlin.

The Giants ended up tying with the Commanders after late mistakes from both offensive units kept the game from having a definitive winner.

Skattebo's fumble with two minutes remaining in overtime cost the Giants the chance to complete an incredible comeback win in overtime.

Mike Tomlin slams Cam Skattebo for wasting 'precious' chance to win against Washington Commanders

Speaking on NBC Sports after the New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to a tie in their all-important NFC East clash, Mike Tomlin had some harsh words for Cam Skattebo.

He lambasted Skattebo for wasting a chance to win a crucial division game, and said that seeing Skattebo fumble the ball made him physically ill.

Tomlin said: "I describe it as disgusting. Division wins are too precious in the National Football League. I was disgusted by the Skattebo fumble. I threw up in my mouth a little bit at the end of the game.

"It's just tough. We'll never know what happened. The head coach said what he was supposed to say. The quarterback said what he was supposed to say.

"But it's just tough, man. Division wins are very precious. They had one in their hands, and they let it slip."

With close to two minutes remaining in overtime, after the Giants had clawed their way back from a 14-point hole, John Harbaugh's side were in field-goal range.

On a first-down about 23 yards away from the Commanders' end zone, QB Jameis Winston handed the ball off to Skattebo, who tried to carry the ball through the middle to gain more yardage.

Commanders DL Daron Payne knocked the ball out of Skattebo's hands, allowing Shy Tuttle to recover it and give the Commanders possession.

Fortunately for Skattebo and the Giants, the Commanders squandered their chance at a win as Jayden Daniels bizarrely let the clock run out before the Commanders could attempt a game-winning field goal.

After the game, Skattebo admitted that it was his mistake that cost the Giants a chance to win the game and took responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: Liverpool must act fast if they want £21m sensation as major news emerges
articles.summary: Even though the transfer window is shut, Liverpool have been continually linked with a whole host of players. Their squad may be full of solid players but, i...
articles.body:
Even though the transfer window is shut, Liverpool have been continually linked with a whole host of players.

Their squad may be full of solid players but, if a few injuries occur, their depth isn't the best.

That has been proven by the recent injuries suffered to Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak.

With those two and Hugo Ekitike out, Liverpool only have Lewis Koumas for a striker and, while he's done fairly well when called upon, the Reds would still be much better off with a more experienced player as their number nine.

To try and resolve this issue, the Reds have been eyeing up a fair few new players and now, they may have to speed up their chase for one of their long-term targets after one of their Premier League rivals have started to show an interest.

Arsenal are ready to make their move for Gilberto Mora in the January transfer window

One thing that has been high on Liverpool's priority list when looking at new transfers has been that they're young and have plenty of potential to fulfil.

This has been proven by the recent signings of Milos Kerkez, Florian Wirtz and Giovanni Leoni .

Although each of these players are good enough to start for Liverpool, them being able to grow and become even better has been a massive selling point for the Reds.

Because, if for whatever reason the Anfield outfit wants to get rid of them, it's always nice for them to be able to profit.

However, as per a fresh update from El Porvenir , Arsenal could be about to jump ahead of Liverpool in the queue for the Mexico international.

"Premier League side Arsenal have approached Tijuana 's management to open talks about a possible signing of Gilberto Mora next January, while Manchester City's attacking midfielder, Rayan Cherki, is on Paris Saint-Germain's radar," they wrote.

"The Mexican international has a $28 million release clause in his contract and is also attracting interest from Real Madrid, Barcelona, ​​Liverpool, Borussia Dortmund and Benfica."

Liverpool must do everything they can to sign Gilberto Mora

Mora is probably only a player that most fans will have heard of because of the 2026 World Cup.

The Mexican became the second-youngest player to ever feature for his country at the World Cup with only Pele managing to beat him.

He may not have got a goal or assist during the tournament but, upon his return to Tijuana, he's been in the form of his life.

This season alone, the midfielder has featured in seven Ligan MX games for his club and has contributed to six goals.

His versatility is also a key part of his game with the 17-year-old able to play as a number 10 or a left-winger.

From the 14 October, he'll be 18 years old which will mean that he'll be able to join any club he wants so, by January, there's likely to be a huge bidding war for him.

If Liverpool are serious about getting a deal over the line for Mora , which they should be, they need to act fast because, if they don't, they'll almost certainly miss out on him.

articles.title: Will Lankshear: The 'Kane-esque' striker Spurs may regret letting go
articles.summary: Will Lankshear's positioning, finishing and poacher's instinct have made him an instant hit at Riverside Stadium – and a cause of lament at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
articles.body:
Leaping high, six yards out, to nod in Tommy Conway's cross from the left wing, Will Lankshear notched his ninth goal in 12 games for Middlesbrough.

It is that positioning, finishing and poacher's instinct, earning Boro a 1-0 win against Wolves on Saturday , that has made Lankshear an instant hit at Riverside Stadium – and a cause of lament at Tottenham Hotspur .

Lankshear joined Boro from Spurs in the summer on a five-year contract in a deal that could rise to a club record buy of £20m.

Since then, he has scored as many goals in all competitions as Spurs' combined team. His old side, despite snatching a draw at Manchester United a few hours after Lankshear's latest winner, remain in the Premier League relegation zone while Boro sit in the Championship's automatic promotion places.

Dominic Solanke's last-minute goal at Old Trafford was the first league goal scored by a Tottenham forward in five months.

It is enough to make Spurs fans despair.

"A lot of fans are wondering why he was sold," Ali Speechly, co-chair of the Women of the Lane supporters' group, told BBC Sport.

"It was likely to do with money - his sell-on price is relatively high, so let's cash in on him.

"I was definitely disappointed. Given how badly we have started this season, as a fan it feels like the wrong decision."

Amid a multi-million pound summer splurge, Spurs allowed Lankshear to leave for an initial fee worth about £10m, with an additional £10m due in add-ons based on various clauses.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Boro content

'Will has an opportunity and he is taking it'

Boro saw off competition around the Championship, and in Europe, to sign the 21-year-old who impressed at Oxford United in the second tier last season, scoring 12 league goals on loan for a relegated side.

Good form for a young player, but not so compelling he had to go straight into the Spurs first team.

"If you are a young kid at a club where you are not getting any first-team football and you get the opportunity to go and play men's football, you should go," former Spurs goalkeeper Paul Robinson told BBC Sport.

"The academies are great and Premier League 2 is a great feeder for the first team, but if you are 21, 22 or 23 and still mostly playing in the under-23s then you have missed the boat.

"Getting first-team football is the best grounding you can get for a young footballer, getting the opportunity to play in the first team, regardless of what league it is. Will has been given this opportunity, and he is taking it."

Lankshear scored 23 goals for Tottenham 's U23 team in the 2023–24 Premier League 2 season and played for the senior side in the 2024-25 Europa League campaign – most notably scoring then getting sent off against Galatasaray .

But amid a churn of players and managers at Spurs, he has moved on – and Boro fans couldn't be happier.

Middlesbrough have built a reputation in recent years of providing a springboard for promising youngsters. Most notably, Morgan Rogers spent six months at Riverside Stadium before joining Aston Villa , and the rest is history.

Not only that, but Boro - who missed out on promotion last season after scoring only once in three play-off games - badly needed a skilful, physical presence who could finish the multitude of chances made by Kim Hellberg's creative but blunt side.

"Boro was a team that made a boatload of chances, and he knew he would be able to get on the end of them," BBC Tees commentator Mark Drury told BBC Sport.

"But what people have been impressed with is his instinctive finishing - one touch, just being in the right place. It's simple but not a lot of people know how to be there at the right time, to give yourself the highest percentage chance.

"He's taller and stockier than he might look from the sidelines, and he is only 21. He seems to have the all-round package - good with both feet and in the air."

A 6ft 2in English striker with a deadly finishing touch, who came through at Spurs before learning his trade in the Football League. Remind you of anyone?

"I can understand the comparisons with Harry Kane," said Robinson. "He has headed down a similar career path to Harry and, physically, he has a similar stature as well.

"Like Kane, he looks like a player who is developing a little later, compared to others who are Premier League regulars before the end of their teens.

"You look at him and the career path he is on; it is a very similar one to the one Harry Kane has been on, and that is a big positive. There is no substitute for playing in the first team somewhere, regardless of what level you are playing at."

Like Kane, Lankshear also had early career setbacks. Initially at Arsenal 's academy, he was released and signed with Sheffield United before being picked up by Spurs for £2m when he was 17.

He also had hit-and-miss loan spells. An unremarkable stint at West Brom was followed by a more fruitful spell with Oxford.

"Harry Kane didn't always have brilliantly successful loan spells, they are not always a marker of a player," says Speechly.

"He didn't do anything remarkable, but it is unfortunate as we are not scoring goals. It is painful to see.

"I don't think we will ever get another Kane, but there are definitely similarities. He is a real poacher and has a strong work ethic. It is very Kane-esque."

Tottenham do not have the right to immediately bring Lankshear back next summer. Clauses in the deal give them the right to be notified of and match any future accepted bid that Middlesbrough receive, and Spurs will get 20% of any profit on any future sale.

They have first refusal rather than a guaranteed, pre-set buy-back, but there remains a feeling Boro are enjoying Lankshear while they can.

"It's just the reality of life, definitely in the Championship but certainly in the Premier League," said Drury. "There is always a pecking order.

"Lankshear seems to have all the tools, including attitude, to make the best of the talent he has got. If he continues at this rate of progress, it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League - hopefully with the Boro."

Such has been Lankshear's form, there has even been talk of a step up from the England under-21s, for who he scored on his debut last month.

Referencing potential punishments for Manchester City , England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was open to calling up players outside the Premier League , external .

If he is succession planning for 33-year-old Kane, given a paucity of top-flight options, a Lankshear call-up may not be so far-fetched.

articles.summary: The Serie A matchday concludes today with Monday’s two fixtures, but the league’s biggest clubs are already looking ahead to their cup commitments and the ne...
articles.body:
The Serie A matchday concludes today with Monday's two fixtures, but the league's biggest clubs are already looking ahead to their cup commitments and the next round of matches.

🚑 Juve's injury crisis continues! Woltemade ready

Following their draw against Cagliari , Juventus are preparing to return to Europa League action: on Thursday, the Bianconeri visit Celta Vigo , aiming to build on their brilliant European opener, a 5-0 thrashing of NEC featuring five different scorers. However, Luciano Spalletti still has a lengthy injury list to contend with: from Yildiz to Locatelli , along with Boga, Ekhator and Thuram, none will recover in time for the trip to Spain. The only player returning will be goalkeeper Neto, who missed the league match through suspension, while Zhegrova is unavailable because he is not on the UEFA squad list.

The absences pave the way for some changes, particularly in defence, where Gatti and Kelly are hoping to start. In attack, Woltemade 's situation remains to be assessed: he has already scored against NEC but is still searching for his first Serie A goal. The German failed to impress in the closing stages against Cagliari, but Spalletti could give him another opportunity in Europe, where Juventus want to continue playing a leading role.

😔 Milan, Cardinale disappointed with Amorim

Gerry Cardinale was at the Mapei Stadium for Sassuolo-Milan, reaffirming his support for the team: Sunday's game was the sixth league match the Rossoneri owner has attended in person. However, according to Sky Sport , the 1-1 draw in Reggio Emilia reportedly fell short of his expectations .

Milan need to show signs of improvement as early as Thursday, when they face Salzburg in the Europa League following their opening defeat to Benfica. Cardinale is reportedly particularly concerned about Amorim 's attacking approach, with Gonçalo Ramos too little involved in the build-up, as well as their defensive frailties and performances at set pieces. After an extended period of work during the break, a more noticeable step forward was expected from the team: now they need to deliver.

🙅‍♂️ Inter turned down two English clubs for Sucic! But without a starting spot...

Zvonimir Boban 's comments have reignited the debate over the future of Petar Sucic , who has so far played less than he expected at Inter. The Dinamo Zagreb president praised the Croatian midfielder, calling him one of the best in the world in his position, and questioned whether staying in Milan would be the right move if the situation does not change. However, according to the well-known Croatian newspaper Sportke Novosti , the player is happy with his experience at Inter and is not considering leaving

His future will depend above all on his playing time over the coming months. Newcastle and Everton had already shown interest in the Croatian, but Inter previously rejected the English clubs' approaches. For his part, Sucic does not want to settle for a peripheral role: he aims to become a regular starter and would only consider other options if he fails to achieve that.

After their win against Frosinone, Napoli are preparing for Tuesday's Champions League trip to Villarreal , aiming to build on the progress shown in the league. According to Corriere dello Sport , Allegri is expected to stick with the 3-4-2-1 , but could make three changes to the starting line-up: Scott McTominay , Billy Gilmour and Matteo Politano are in contention to start after coming off the bench in the match at the Maradona.

The tactical setup remains to be finalised. McTominay could partner Lobotka in central midfield or move into an attacking midfield role, with either Lang or Neres at risk of losing their place; Gilmour, meanwhile, could line up alongside the Slovak, giving De Bruyne more freedom in attacking midfield. There are two options for Politano: play on the right of the four-man midfield, with Di Lorenzo dropping back into defence, or take a more advanced position in place of Neres.

🟥 Roma, how long a ban could Malen face?

Donyell Malen received the first red card of his career, sent off against Como for a dangerous challenge on Kaiki . The Roma striker protested over a foul he had suffered moments earlier, but the referee upheld the dismissal. As Luca Marelli explained on DAZN, the decision was correct: the speed of the challenge, the proximity of the knee and the exposed studs are enough to constitute serious foul play , even though there was no full contact.

The expected punishment is a one-match suspension : Malen will therefore miss Saturday's clash with Genoa , but will be available again for the big match against Napoli. There are no issues, however, for Wednesday's European fixture against Real Madrid , in which the Dutchman will be free to lead Roma's attack.

🤔 Lazio heading to the Stadium without organised supporter groups?

The trip to face Juventus has already drawn a strong response from Lazio fans: all 1,016 seats in the lower tier of the away section at the Allianz Stadium have sold out. According to Il Tempo , tickets remain available for the upper tier, which offers another 2,099 seats. The number of Lazio supporters in Turin could therefore increase over the coming days, in contrast to the ongoing protest involving some fans at home matches at the Stadio Olimpico.

However, the position of the organised supporter groups remains unclear, as they have not yet announced whether they will follow the team on the trip. Ticket sales already confirm a significant turnout, but do not yet resolve the question of whether the organised groups will be present at the Allianz Stadium. A decision is expected in the coming days.

🎯 Fiorentina had two big names in their midfield sights

Midfield remains one of the issues Fiorentina need to address. As Corriere Fiorentino points out, the summer plans focused on the quality of Fagioli, Oulai and Atta , but the idea of relying on a technically gifted midfield must be balanced against the need for greater defensive cover and stability. Atta's injury further complicates matters, with the player set to remain sidelined for some time.

That is why, in the closing stages of the summer transfer window, Fabio Paratici tried to act, sounding out players such as Torreira, Thorstvedt and Brozovic , after Grosso had identified Matic and Hojbjerg as two potential reinforcements. However, no deal was completed and the issue remained unresolved, carrying over from Grosso's tenure to that of current coach Vanoli . The club must now assess how to give their midfield greater solidity.

articles.body: Raphinha sigue en lo más alto de la clasificación del Pichichi como máximo goleador de LaLiga EA Sports tras la jornada 8. El brasileño, que volvió lesionado de Brasil, no jugó ante el Getafe y sigue consolidado con 12 tantos como máximo realizador de Primera. Ninguno de sus perseguidores más cercanos fue capaz de ver portería y, por tanto, el brasileño mantiene la ventaja. Camello, Lamine Yamal y Mbappé se mantienen con siete dianas tras quedarse a cero en la primera jornada después del largo parón de selecciones. Sólo Ante Budimir, de Osasuna, y Yassir Zabiri, del Racing de Santander, se acercaron un poco más a ese grupo de cabeza que persigue al capitán del Barcelona. Sus equipos no pudieron ganar, pero ambos ya llevan 6 goles en este curso. En el resto de Premios MARCA destaca el Miguel Muñoz, que otorga el premio a mejor entrenador de la temporada, que sigue liderando Hansi Flick con 20 puntos. Cierran el podio Antonio Hidalgo, del Deportivo, con 16, y Quique Sánchez Flores, del Alavés, con 15.

articles.title: La primera gran 'faena' de Morante con el Betis
articles.standfirst: El canterano se estrena en Primera división con un golazo y lo celebra toreando de salón
articles.summary: El canterano se estrena en Primera división con un golazo y lo celebra toreando de salón
articles.body: José Antonio Morante, hijo de la leyenda del toreo Morante de la Puebla, vivió ayer su primera gran tarde como jugador del Betis. En su memoria quedará el día del debut, el pasado mes de enero en Salónica, en un partido de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Europa League frente al PAOK. Pero este domingo, ante Osasuna, se estrenó en La Cartuja con el primer equipo verdiblanco y dejó su sello con un golazo que celebró toreando de salón sobre el césped. Su primera gran 'faena'. La historia de Morante con el Betis tiene, además, algo de capricho del destino. El joven futbolista, de 19 años de edad, no consiguió superar su primera prueba en la cantera verdiblanca y tuvo que buscarse la vida en el Coria, donde sus actuaciones volvieron a despertar el interés de los ojeadores. El Granada fue el primero en dar el paso para incorporarlo, pero una circunstancia muy particular terminó cambiando el rumbo de su carrera: su padre tenía compromisos taurinos durante la Feria de Abril y no podía acompañarlo para cerrar su fichaje por el conjunto nazarí. "Torea mi padre miércoles, corta el rabo en Sevilla y el jueves me llama el Betis. Imagínate la felicidad de un niño que siempre ha ido al estadio y que siempre ha disfrutado de esa afición", recordó el canterano bético hace unos días en una entrevista para Made in Betis. Una curiosa carambola que permitió al club verdiblanco incorporar a un talento que, a pasos agigantados, empieza a hacerse un sitio no solo en el club de su vida sino también a nivel internacional, brillando con las categorías inferiores de la Selección Española. Ante el conjunto rojillo, apenas necesitó unos minutos para demostrar su talento. Saltó al césped en el 92' sustituyendo a Abde. Y poco después, recibió un balón entre líneas y, sin pensárselo dos veces, soltó un latigazo con la zurda desde fuera del área que tras rozar en un rival se coló en la portería de Aitor Fernández. Primer partido en LaLiga, primera vez que se mostraba en La Cartuja con los mayores y primer gol para un jugador llamado a escribir páginas de éxito en el club heliopolitano. "No me lo creo. Estoy que se me sale el corazón por la boca", acertaba a decir Morante con los ojos vidriosos tras su sensacional debut liguero. "He hecho lo que me decía el míster. Me dijo que una iba a tener. La que he tenido y ha ido para dentro. A disfrutar...", añadía. Y a continuación, explicaba cómo fue ese primer gol con el Betis: "He visto que iba Héctor, también Troy... el control ha sido bueno y gracias a Dios ha entrado. ¿Un paso más en mi carrera? Totalmente. Hay que seguir trabajando en el día a día, espero que sigan llegando las oportunidades y aprovecharlas". Al joven Morante se le pasaron muchas cosas por la cabeza: "El niño que fue de pequeño al campo en un partido contra el Real Madrid, cuando fui a un Betis-Alcorcón o los momentos que he pasado de pequeño con la familia en el estadio". Y ahora, lanzado tras su prometedor estreno, ya piensa "en la Champions"... "De donde venimos a jugar la Champions... hay que disfrutar al máximo de todos estos momentos", finalizó el futbolista sevillano. El gol de Morante, además, fue uno de los más rápidos de un jugador del Betis desde su debut en Primera división. Como informó MisterChip en la red social X, sólo Pancrate, que marcó contra el Athletic Club a los dos minutos y 49 segundos, y Kowalczyk, que lo hizo ante el Sporting a los tres minutos, mejoran los tres minutos y 29 segundos sobre el césped que necesitó el canterano bético para estrenarse como goleador en Primera división ante Osasuna. En el Betis, con Pellegrini al frente, se han encargado en estos meses de cuidar al detalle todos los pasos en la carrera de Morante, para evitar que una exposición prematura en la élite pudiera cortar su progresión. Su presencia en las pretemporadas y sus participaciones puntuales en los entrenamientos del primer equipo se han convertido ya en una participación constante en el trabajo con los mayores, esperando el momento perfecto para su debut liguero. Después de 13 partidos internacionales con la sub 19, con cinco goles, el otro día le tocó estrenarse con la sub 20, también marcando. Ahora llega su turno en el Betis, donde está llamado a grandes éxitos. Pero con la calma que exige el salto y un futuro garantizado en el club tras su renovación hasta 2030. "Es un jugador que lo tiene todo: joven, con mucha proyección, mucha calidad, muy buen tiro y está en el equipo perfecto para crecer de la mejor manera posible. Tenemos que cuidarlo entre todos y seguro que nos va a ayudar mucho", dijo Isco, que sabe de qué va esto...

articles.title: Can Robinson solve Aberdeen's lack of goals?
articles.summary: Aberdeen draw a blank again in Sunday's home loss to St Johnstone, but manager Stephen Robinson is sure his team can find a solution.
articles.body:
Aberdeen legend Willie Miller summed up the Dons' home defeat by St Johnstone on Sunday as "depressing".

Although they dominated possession and had 22 shots at goal, there was a feeling they could have played all night and not scored.

Stephen Robinson's side have scored just seven goals in the first eight league games of the new season, with four of them in a 4-0 rout of Motherwell. This was their fifth blank.

Robinson insists he can reverse their woes in front of goal, but the manager must act fast to ensure it does not become a fatal flaw.

St Johnstone defeat blunt Aberdeen to reach top six

Visit our Aberdeen page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Get Aberdeen news notifications in the BBC Sport app

Miller delivered his damning verdict on the final whistle, as the home fans who remained until the end jeered their beleaguered team.

"Very little was done when Aberdeen had the ball, and St Johnstone didn't have to think too much about defending. It got so predictable," Miller said.

Indeed, the hosts had 65% possession and attempted a season-high number of shots and passes.

However, the quality of both were poor and Toby Steward in the St Johnstone goal only had two impressive saves to make.

"The centre-backs were playing long balls," Miller added. "They had three wide players and couldn't punch holes in a St Johnstone side who are not noted for their defence.

The lack of creativity was stark. Although substitutes Lewis Smith, Tony Yogane and Hicham Mahou - making his Aberdeen debut - did get involved, far too many crosses either sailed over red heads or failed to beat the first man.

Attacking stats confirm creative worries

Aberdeen aren't alone in their barren run. Falkirk and Kilmarnock are both on seven goals scored from eight, but the Dons' targets will be far loftier given their superior budget.

Their xG is just 8.3 - the lowest in the league - so they aren't missing lots of chances either.

Just 2.9 shots on target per match stands alone as the worst record across the division, while the 12 big chances they have created across eight games is another joint-low.

One frustration against St Johnstone was they did have two big chances, and one fell to the man they would want it to.

Kevin Nisbet was put one-on-one by a brilliant through ball, but the striker seemed to panic and had his shot easily saved.

Nisbet has netted 43% of the team's league goals - three of seven - from just five shots on target.

"Outwith Kevin Nisbet, we're not scoring enough goals," Robinson admitted post-match. "We need people to step up."

Aberdeen must 'be brave' to break barren hoodoo

The head coach admitted his side have an issue, but was also adamant in his resolve that his players can find a solution.

"What I see in training is that we have that quality," Robinson said. "We've not been able to convert that.

"It's the hardest bit of the game. You see teams like Rangers and Celtic struggling to break down teams that sit deep. We're no different.

"There's no hiding place. Our last pass, last decision, wasn't what I know it can be today."

Fans may point to St Mirren's lack of goals under Robinson last season. The Buddies scored 30 across the campaign - the worst record in the league by 10 goals - although it must be noted Robinson departed in March to take over at Pittodrie.

The season before, when the Northern Irishman guided the Paisley Saints to a third consecutive top-six finish, they scored more goals than Aberdeen and Dundee United - who also finished in the top half.

Those impressive returns were also often done without a proven, consistent goalscorer in the St Mirren ranks.

It's not a problem that has plagued him before, so perhaps Robinson can find the answer. Perhaps his side is simply missing a bit of "good fortune", as Miller pointed out on Sportsound.

Robinson's mettle is certainly not in doubt, with the manager adding: "Do I believe they can? Yeah, but we have to be brave to do that."

Darren : Zero goals at home again, against a newly promoted club, following a goalless draw with bottom club Kilmarnock. There's absolutely no joy in watching Aberdeen anymore, we've forgotten how to play football and score goals. There's a brand new team every year. Something is broken, and loyal fans deserve so much more than what Robinson is serving up.

Neil : Three centre halves at home to St Johnstone, with no wingers and no pace. Was always going to be a struggle. Don't create chances and the few we do, we are not clinical enough. Very poor.

Alan : Robinson keeps harping on about what he sees in training but what he doesn't appreciate is, it's mediocrity versus dross. Any modestly-equipped player will look good. Bottom line, we are mediocre at best having signed no quality.

Robert : It's just not good enough. To say Rangers and Celtic struggle to break down teams is a pathetic excuse. The difference is they do break down teams that sit in to get three points. Aberdeen are just simply clueless when it comes down to having the quality pass or movement. At this rate, a top six finish is beyond us.

Graham : Nowhere near good enough from the players. No quality in front of goal and still clearly need a number nine. Robinson needs to accept his part in this weekly dross but the players need to play for Aberdeen and each other.

John : To say the team's display was disappointing is an understatement. We were absolutely awful. St Johnstone did enough to stop us from scoring. Afraid our cash is being spent on quantity and not quality. A lot of problems from the top down.

articles.title: Clarence Seedorf: Corinthians hire former Netherlands midfielder as head coach
articles.summary: Brazilian club Corinthians appoint Clarence Seedorf as their head coach, with the former Netherlands midfielder taking on his first coaching role since 2019.
articles.body:
Corinthians have appointed Clarence Seedorf as their head coach, with the former Netherlands midfielder taking on his first coaching role since 2019.

The 50-year-old has joined on a contract until the end of 2027 with the club 16th in the Brazilian top flight, one place above the relegation zone with eight games left.

Seedorf succeeds former Brazil interim national coach Fernando Diniz, who was sacked by Corinthians last week after the club lost seven consecutive league games.

Seedorf's last coaching role was with the Cameroon national team more than seven years ago, while he has previously had underwhelming spells at AC Milan, Shenzhen FC and Deportivo La Coruna.

"Taking on this challenge is an honour, but also a huge responsibility. I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory," said Seedorf of his Corinthians appointment.

Seedorf inherits a Corinthians squad which features former Manchester United players Memphis Depay and Jesse Lingard.

Dutch great Seedorf retired from playing in 2014 following a glittering career which yielded four Champions League titles - two with AC Milan, one with Real Madrid and one with Ajax.

Seedorf remains the only player to win the Champions League with three different clubs.

articles.title: Declan Rice: Mikel Arteta says Arsenal midfielder has transitioned away from his 'lighthouse' role, so what is he?
articles.summary: Declan Rice is no longer a 'lighthouse' player, according to Mikel Arteta - so what does the Arsenal manager mean by that? Rice is more active in attack this season; watch Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports Premier League this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
"I went to him and I said: 'You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else,'" the Arsenal manager revealed after the 2-1 win over Leeds, after Rice set up Bruno Guimaraes' winner.

"At the end of the season, I can tell you what [and] where I want to take him. But he's not the lighthouse anymore, he's something else and he needs to prove that on the pitch."

For those confused about what football and light towers have in common, Rice was previously heralded as the 'lighthouse' of the Arsenal team.

"Somebody who brings a focal point, clarity and direction to everybody," said Arteta last season. "You look at him and you know where to head."

The lighthouse tag followed Rice everywhere after he joined Arsenal in 2023. It was the same term Pep Guardiola used to describe Rodri at Manchester City.

"Guardiola tells me to be the coach on the field. He compares my position to that of a lighthouse," said the former City midfielder, now at Barcelona. "Don't move, let everything revolve around you."

It sounds like a traditional defensive midfielder position, focused on an off-the-ball influence. But those days are over. Rice has a new role in this team - and this season has heralded a new version of Rice.

When it comes to improvement one area stands out from the Arsenal and England man so far this term - his passing ability in open play.

In six league games this season, Rice has three assists from open play, more than he managed in the entire of the 2025/26 Premier League campaign. And not only that, but all three of those assists are similar.

Two of them were for Guimaraes goals against Sunderland and Leeds - both set up the Brazilian from outside the box, both set up long-range goals, both put Arsenal in front during sticky situations.

The other assist was a quick ball through the lines for Kai Havertz's goal against Chelsea. Again, that was a strike that generated space for the German to shoot from outside the box. Again, that equaliser got Arsenal out of a tricky hole.

All of these moments are part of a wider picture that Rice has gone up a level in possession, showing a dramatic improvement in terms of attacking influence on the ball.

Rice is playing more of an active role in the final third of the pitch this season. The number of final-third entries he has averaged this season has gone up by 25 per cent compared to last season. That figure has also doubled since the 2024/25 campaign.

Rice has also made far more passes in the final third of the pitch than last season, while the number of line-breaking passes he has averaged this season has once again nearly doubled.

He is finding gaps between the opposition players more often - so much so that he has made more line-breaking passes than any other Premier League player. He is more than just a defensive midfielder focused on off-the-ball protection.

This has been a clear shift in terms of Rice's output from open play, which was often criticised for passing sideways and backwards far too often. Well, he has improved in that discipline too.

Not only has Rice's forward passing numbers gone up - but the number of backwards passes he averages has gone down by 50 per cent.

That reduction in backwards passes is to be expected given Rice has also undergone a positional change at Arsenal.

He now sits more at the base of the Arsenal midfield - allowing for Myles Lewis-Skelly and Guimaraes to have a greater effect going forward. That contrasts massively to the 'left eight' role he used to have.

But there are still moments - such as Rice's backheel assist for Guimaraes' winner against Leeds - where he still impacts the penalty area. And it creates a wider point about the midfielder's new role: the old version Rice still exists.

He still makes those tactically fascinating runs forward to create chaos. He still carries the ball forward with lung-bursting runs that we've seen in previous seasons. He is still that set piece threat from corners.

But Rice has now added open play passing to his and Arteta's Arsenal. He can crash the penalty box but also sit in front of the back four. He is effective in the dead ball and open play scenarios.

Many wanted a new type of Arsenal from the efficient, defensive, set-piece-influenced team that won the Premier League last season.

But Rice is summing up this slightly different Arsenal. Like Rice's assist numbers, all of Arsenal's goals are from open play. They haven't scored from a set piece since March.

Arsenal are evolving. Rice, at the heart of the team, is evolving with them.

articles.title: La plantilla ya se centra en la Juventus: "Estamos muy ilusionados con Europa"
articles.standfirst: Los célticos necesitan puntuar en la competición continental tras la derrota inesperada en Chipre ante el Omonia Nicosia
articles.summary: Los célticos necesitan puntuar en la competición continental tras la derrota inesperada en Chipre ante el Omonia Nicosia
articles.body: Aparca el Celta durante cuatro días la competición liguera para centrarse en la Europa League y en la visita de la Juventus, más de 26 años después, a Balaídos. Un partido muy atractivo y esperado. Más allá de lo llamativo del choque, los célticos tienen necesidad de sumar en el torneo continental después de la derrota inesperada en Chipre ante el Omonia Nicosia. Claudio Giráldez seguirá sin poder contar con los tres futbolistas lesionados y a los cuales les restan semanas para poder reaparecer: Miguel Román, Carl Starfelt y Jones-El Abdellaoui. Lo normal es que repita la convocatoria de Elche con las ya habituales rotaciones del técnico en el once. La plantilla desea la llegada del partido ante la Juve, como señala Ferran Jutglà: “Estamos muy ilusionados con Europa. Ahora a preparar bien el partido ante la Juventus y después ya pensaremos en el Alavés". Aleix Febas, a su vez, tiene un mensaje para la afición céltica que llenará en la noche del jueves el estadio vigués: “Le pedimos que esté con nosotros porque, como siempre, lo daremos todo y creo que veremos un partido muy bonito en Balaídos”. Yoel Lago también se refiere al choque continental: “El equipo está muy ilusionado con este partido, pero tenemos que darle la misma importancia que a todos e ir a por los tres puntos”.

articles.title: Manchester City: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher warn of Premier League 'stain' if resolution on financial charges is not found
articles.summary: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher say a ‘stain’ hangs over Man City until their financial charges are resolved, despite their win over Liverpool taking them top of the Premier League; Man City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield in their first game since guilty veredict
articles.body:
City's victory at Liverpool on Sunday, which hinged on Ryan Gravenberch's controversial dismissal, took them back to the top of the Premier League.

But the win was inevitably overshadowed after the independent Premier League commission found Manchester City in breach of the Premier League's financial rules - City have denied wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal - with Sky Sports commentator Peter Drury describing the game as "the most peculiar day in Premier League history".

"We're sat here not knowing what it means," reflected Gary Neville. "City supporters will be delighted [with the win], but I don't think they recognise right now the stain, the stigma and the damage this is going to do to them.

"Liverpool fans are singing 'going down', they're shouting 'cheats' and you can't get away from that."

Jamie Carragher added: "In some ways, the feeling around Manchester City will only grow the more they win. It will keep growing and growing around the country. We need a resolution as soon as possible. We're watching a game today, but what does it actually mean?"

'Cheat' banners were unfurled by both sets of fans, with every touch by a City player greeted by a chant of 'cheat' in the final minutes.

"There was a banner over in that far corner which I thought was devastating - 'A generation of supporters have been cheated'. I thought you know, that will be the mood around the country, that for 10-15 years they've been cheated," said Neville on his podcast.

"We should be absolutely eulogising over a performance like that, where they've come through and withstood a really difficult opening spell - which is always the case here at Anfield - and then gone on to come out on top.

"But there's a 'but', isn't there? And we're sat here not knowing what this means.

"We know that Manchester City go three points clear at the top of the league but there's a feeling that ultimately this is not going to be where Manchester City finish.

"It does feel different. There is a 'but', there is a sort of shadow hanging over it - there's a dark cloud that you know has got a load of rain in it, and a massive storm, and you just don't know when it's going to burst but you know it's coming."

articles.title: "El fútbol español está herido de muerte"
articles.standfirst: José Luis Sánchez se muestra muy crítico en La Tribu con el arbitraje del Real Madrid-Villarreal y la expulsión de Vinicius
articles.summary: José Luis Sánchez se muestra muy crítico en La Tribu con el arbitraje del Real Madrid-Villarreal y la expulsión de Vinicius
articles.body: José Luis Sánchez, Antonio Sanz, Ricardo Rosety, Yon Cuezva, Emilio Pérez de Rozas y Fernando Kallás han sido los tertulianos de este lunes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por la expulsión de Vinicius ante el Villarreal y la posible sanción que le hará perderse el Clásico, el gran momento del Barcelona y el regreso de la Champions. José Luis Sánchez. "El fútbol español está herido de muerte. Lo que vimos el sábado es impropio de un arbitraje de élite. El problema no es la expulsión, sino los criterios. De 104 partidos en el Mundial, solo hubo un árbitro español. Hay que esperar a las sanciones por el caso Negreira. Esto es insostenible. No creo en el fútbol español. A Vinicius le patean en la primera jornada de Liga y no pasa nada, a Mbappé le abren la nariz la temporada pasada y no pasa nada, a Mbappé casi le parten la pierna en Cornellá y no pasa nada". Antonio Sanz. "No hubo error arbitral en la expulsión. Es recurrente que cada fin de semana la afición del Real Madrid se queje de los árbitros. Estamos ante la peor generación arbitral que yo recuerdo. Los arbitrajes, en general, son calamitosos, lamentables. Los árbitros cada jornada empeoran". Ricardo Rosety: "La jugada de Vinicius tiene poca discusión, es roja. Cada fin de semana, en cada partido del Madrid, se pone el foco en los árbitros. Solo se fijan en el saldo en contra. Estar hablando de Negreira hoy en día y pensar que estos árbitros siguen afectados por ese caso, que está judicializado, ayuda a emborronar y embarrar los debates". Yon Cuezva. "Estamos viviendo, a 12 de octubre, en un estado de histeria absoluto que está fuera de lugar. Me parece demencial. Se intenta generar un relato arbitral de que el Madrid es un equipo perjudicado por los árbitros. La jugada de la expulsión es clarísima". Emilio Pérez de Rozas. "El Madrid tiene un pollo ahí dentro de narices. Mourinho está deseando que hablemos de esto y no de cómo juega su equipo. El espectáculo de Mourinho en el banquillo fue tremendo. Ahí dentro va a pasar algo, en la presidencia, con el entrenador o con los futbolistas. Mourinho está en los últimos coletazos como personaje y como meme. Fernando Kallás. "La jugada es clara, Vinicius está bien expulsado. Su suplencia es merecida, Vinicius no está bien, ni técnica ni físicamente".
